newsitem.title: GERMANY: BT, Viag win German mobile licence.
newsitem.headline: BT, Viag win German mobile licence.

text.p: The German government on Tuesday awarded a consortium owned by British Telecom Plc and utility Viag AG the country's fourth mobile telephone licence.

German Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch said the E2 Mobilfunk GmbH consortium was the only group to apply for the licence but assured it was put through a rigourous technical examination before receiving a concession.

"In the interest of consumers current mobile phone operators Deutsche Telekom MobilNet, Mannesmann Mobilfunk and E-Plus Mobilfunk have receive another competitor," he said in a statement prepared for delivery at a news conference.
E2 Mobilfunk can begin construction of the network immediately and it must make its services available to at least 75 percent of the population by the end of 2001.

BT and Viag have said in the past that they intended to build the network in phases. In the first stages they would concentrate on key economic centres and only later expand the network to less populated areas.

The licence is for Germany's second mobile phone network based on the DCS 1800 personal communications network (PCN) standard. The first PCN is operated by the E-Plus group owned by Veba, Thyssen, BellSouth and Vodafone. E-Plus has around 500,000 subscribers.
There are also two other digital networks based on the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) standard.
Deutsche Telekom's D1 network has around 2.2 million subscribers.
Mannesmann Mobilfunk, owned by engineering group Mannesmann AG and AirTouch Communications of the United States has around 2.3 million subscribers.
